transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not making a fuss over nothing, I know you must be very busy with people who have much bigger problems. 

But... well, I guess what finally scared me enough to ask for help is... I've been having these mornings lately. And it's a bit embarrassing to admit, I know I shouldn't think this way, but sometimes I just lie there and think... maybe it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. 

I don't have any sort of plan to hurt myself, I promise you that! I would never actually do anything like that, ever. But just having that thought pop into my head... it frightened me a little bit. I hope it's alright that I came in to talk about it. Does that... does that make sense?
Can you tell me more about how you've been feeling lately? Have you noticed a change in your mood or interest in things you used to enjoy?

Well, um... I suppose things have been a little different lately. I don't want to sound like a complainer, because I know I'm very fortunate. But my mood has just been... a bit flat, I guess you could say. 

As for my interests, I'm still keeping up with everything! I really am. I still make myself show up for things like my book club, and the weekly dance night at the community center. I wouldn't want to let anyone down by not being there. But... lately, I sit there and I just feel sort of... disconnected. Like I'm behind a pane of glass, watching everyone else have a good time. 

And, well, usually I love my garden, and I always enjoy cooking little treats for the neighbors. But even those things just... they don't give me that little lift they used to. I just go through the motions. I feel terrible even saying that out loud, it sounds so ungrateful, doesn't it? I hope you don't think poorly of me for feeling this way. I'm trying my best to stay active, I really am. Is it normal to feel like that sometimes?
Have you noticed that your mood has been low or that you’ve had a hard time enjoying things for most of the day, on most days lately?

Well, yes, I suppose it has been most days... for about a month now. I really hope I'm not making too much out of it, but... well, it started right around the time my sister passed away. It was very unexpected, and... oh, I'm sorry, I know people lose loved ones all the time and manage just fine. I should be handling it better, shouldn't I? I just... I haven't quite been myself since then. But I am trying to push through it, I promise. Is it okay that it's taking me a little while to bounce back?
Can you tell me if you’ve noticed a loss of pleasure or interest in most activities, even ones you used to enjoy?

Oh, um... I think we might have just talked about that a little bit, didn't we? I hope I didn't confuse things by jumping ahead earlier. 

But yes, like I was saying, I still do everything I'm supposed to do. I still go to my groups and I still keep my garden tidy. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself! It's just... I don't feel that same spark of joy from them right now. I'm sure it will come back eventually, though. I just need to keep trying, right? I'm doing the right thing by keeping up with my activities, aren't I, Doctor?
Doctor: Have you found that your mood has been down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, rather than just having moments where you feel this way?

Well, um... I suppose it is most of the day, yes. It's not just a passing moment here or there. It's sort of a... a quiet heaviness that just sits with me from the time I wake up until I go to bed. 

But I want to be clear, I'm not crying all day or anything like that! I'm still getting dressed and keeping the house neat. I don't want you to picture me just moping around in my pajamas from dawn till dusk. I'm trying very hard to keep a brave face, especially when the neighbors stop by. It's just... underneath it all, that low feeling is pretty much always there right now. I hope I'm explaining that right... does that make sense, Doctor?
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or have trouble sitting still and feel restless lately?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm certainly not as spry as I was in my twenties, but I keep up with my chores just fine! I make sure to get my steps in around the house, and I certainly don't just sit around fidgeting or anything like that. I try to stay very composed. 

I suppose maybe I take a little longer to get up from my chair sometimes, but that's just normal for my age, isn't it? I don't think I'm moving unusually slow or acting restless... I'm doing okay in that department, right? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers, Doctor.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired than usual, even if you haven't been doing anything physically demanding?

Well, um... I suppose I have been a little more tired lately. But it's really nothing to worry about! I mean, I'm still keeping up with my responsibilities. 

It's just... sometimes, even simple errands, or, you know, getting the papers together for my groups at the Cultural Center... it leaves me feeling a bit worn out. Almost like my body is moving through thick mud, if that makes sense? But I push through it! I make sure everything gets done, I promise. I'm just getting a little older, so it's natural to need a bit more rest, right? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm complaining or being lazy, Doctor. I really am trying my best to stay active.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately?

Well, um... I suppose my appetite hasn't been quite what it usually is. But it's nothing drastic, really! I'm certainly not starving myself or anything like that. 

It's just that... well, food just doesn't call to me much anymore. I'll fix myself a little piece of toast or maybe heat up some soup, and then... well, I'll realize by the evening that I've barely eaten anything all day. I'm definitely not trying to lose weight or go on any sort of diet, I promise. It just slips my mind to eat a full meal sometimes. That's fairly normal when you live alone and don't have a big family to cook for anymore, isn't it? I hope you don't think I'm neglecting my health, Doctor. I really am trying to make sure I get something in my stomach every day.
Have you been feeling like you're not good enough or that you've let people down, even when you've done your best?

Oh, goodness... well, I suppose everyone feels a little regret now and then, don't they? It's just a normal part of life. I certainly don't sit around feeling sorry for myself all day, I promise you that. 

But... well, I have been thinking a lot about the last few weeks with my sister. I just... I keep going over it in my head, telling myself I really should have called her more often. Or maybe I should have listened better when we did talk, or done something, anything, more useful for her. I mean, a small part of me knows that I probably couldn't have changed what happened... but I still feel like I let her down. I should have been better. 

But I'm sure that's just a normal reaction, isn't it? It doesn't mean there's something terribly wrong with me, does it, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm not overreacting or being too sensitive about it all.
Doctor: Have you felt this way — that heaviness you described — every day, even on days when nothing particularly sad was happening?

Oh, well... no, I wouldn't say it's *every* single day. I mean, I'm sure I have some good days mixed in there, right? I try to keep my spirits up, I really do! 

I suppose... well, maybe it does linger in the background quite a bit, even when there's no real reason for it. Like on a nice sunny afternoon, I might still feel a little... sluggish, I guess you could say. But I don't let it ruin my day! I still get up and make my tea and try to stay positive. It's not like I'm crying all the time or anything like that. That would just be silly of me, wouldn't it? I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm making a mountain out of a molehill, Doctor. I'm just trying to answer as honestly as I can.
Would you say that this tiredness or lack of energy has been present most days, even when you haven’t been doing anything particularly strenuous?

Oh, goodness... well, I wouldn't want you to think I just sit around the house doing nothing all day! I really do try to keep myself busy and stay active. 

But... I suppose, yes, I have been feeling a bit more tired than usual lately. It's the strangest thing, really. Even just running simple errands, or... well, getting my papers together for the Cultural Center, which usually isn't hard at all... it just leaves me feeling completely worn out. It almost feels like my body is moving through thick mud, if that makes any sense? 

But I'm sure that's just a normal part of getting a little older, isn't it? I mean, you can't expect to have boundless energy at my age! I just hope you don't think I'm being lazy or making excuses, Doctor. I really do try my best to push through it and get things done.
Can you recall if there have been times recently when even things you used to enjoy completely lost their appeal, not just that they didn’t bring as much joy as before?

Oh, well... I certainly don't want to sound ungrateful, Doctor. I really do try to keep up with all my activities! I still make myself show up for things, you know, like my book club, or the dance night. I'd hate to be a bother or have people think I'm just giving up on my social life. 

But... if I'm being completely honest with you... lately, when I'm at those things, I just sit there feeling like... well, like I'm behind a pane of glass. It's the strangest feeling. And even my garden, which I usually just adore, or cooking a nice little meal for the neighbors... they just don't give me that little lift they used to. I still do them, of course! I really do. But the appeal just seems to have faded away entirely. 

I suppose it's perfectly normal to get a bit bored of a routine every now and then, though, isn't it? I just hope I don't sound terribly pessimistic to you. I really am trying my best to stay engaged with everyone, I promise. That's alright, isn't it?
Have you found that activities you used to enjoy have completely lost their appeal, as if you can’t enjoy them at all anymore?

Oh, um... well, didn't we just touch on that a little bit? I mean, I don't want to repeat myself and waste your time, Doctor. 

But, yes, as I was saying... I still do all the things I'm supposed to do. I don't just sit around moping! But... yes, I suppose the actual enjoyment of them is... well, it's just not there right now. Like I can't feel the fun of it, even though I know I should. But I'm still trying, I really am! I just don't want you to think I've given up on everything. That makes sense, doesn't it?
Would you say that your low mood has been present most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Oh, goodness, no... I wouldn't say it's been every day, or even most of the day. I really would hate for you to think I'm just walking around with a dark cloud over my head all the time complaining! I really do try my hardest to keep my spirits up and, you know, count my blessings. 

I mean, I do have moments where I feel a bit... well, a bit blue, I suppose. But it certainly isn't an all-day affair. I still have perfectly fine parts of my day, and there are days where I feel quite alright. It definitely hasn't been a constant, heavy thing for two whole weeks straight. I always try to focus on the positive and put on a brave face... I think that's the best way to handle things, don't you agree?
Would you say that your low mood has been present most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Oh, dear, I hope I didn't confuse you just a moment ago! I am so sorry if I wasn't being clear enough before. 

But, um, no... just like I was trying to say, it really hasn't been that constant. Not most of the day, and certainly not for two whole weeks in a row. I would feel just dreadful if you thought I was sitting around being miserable day in and day out! I really do have plenty of good hours where I feel perfectly fine and keep myself busy. 

I hope I'm answering your questions properly... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is that a bit clearer now?
Can you think back and tell me if there was a time in the past few weeks when you felt down or low most of the day, nearly every day, for a period of at least two weeks straight?

Oh, my... I feel terrible, I really must be doing a poor job of explaining myself today. I'm so sorry, Doctor, I don't mean to make you ask the same thing over and over! 

But, um... no, really, I can't think of any time like that. I haven't had any stretch where I was feeling down most of the day, every day, for two weeks. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or hide anything from you! I just... I really do try to stay cheerful, and I haven't had a long period like that where I couldn't shake it off. I hope I'm not frustrating you... I'm doing my best to be helpful, really I am.
Looking back, can you recall if there was ever a time when you felt down or low most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks straight?

Oh my... I feel just awful that we keep coming back to this. I really must be doing a terrible job of answering you, and I am so, so sorry. I feel like I'm failing a test or being difficult, and I promise you I don't want to be a bother! 

But... no, honestly, even looking way back, I just can't recall a time like that. I've never had a spell where I felt low for two whole weeks without a break. I've always made sure to keep busy and keep my chin up, you know? I really hope you believe me—I wouldn't hide anything from you, I promise! 

Is there... is there something specific you're looking for me to say? I really just want to make sure I'm doing this right for you.

Looking back at the time after your sister passed away, was there a period lasting at least two weeks where your low mood was at its worst — where you felt emotionally numb, lost pleasure completely, and maybe even felt worse in the mornings?

Oh... my sister. Yes, well, of course that was a terribly sad time. I miss her so much. But, um... oh dear, I feel like I'm disappointing you again because I'm going to have to say no to that, too. 

Even right after she passed, I wasn't... I wasn't completely numb or entirely without joy for two whole weeks. I still made sure to find little things to appreciate, like a nice cup of tea or a phone call with a friend. And my mornings... well, I always, always got up and got dressed right away. I didn't want to just fall apart and let myself go—I'd hate to be a burden or a worry to anyone, you know? I really tried my best to keep a brave face through it all. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm just trying to be as honest as I can so I don't give you the wrong impression... I really hope I'm being helpful.
Looking back over the past few months, can you think of any time when you felt down or low most of the day, nearly every day, for a period of two weeks or more?

Oh, dear... I feel like we're going in circles, and I just know it's my fault for not being clear enough. I'm so sorry, Doctor. I really, truly don't mean to be difficult or evasive. I know you're just trying to help me, and I appreciate that so much.

But... looking back over the last few months... no, I really haven't had a time like that. Not for two whole weeks, anyway. I mean, everyone has a bad day here and there, don't they? But I always try to snap out of it quickly. I'd never want to let myself wallow and become a nuisance to the people around me. I always try to look on the bright side and keep myself busy. 

I'm answering this right, aren't I? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. I promise I'm not trying to hide anything... I just genuinely haven't felt that way.
Looking back over the past few months, was there ever a period where you felt down or low most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Oh, goodness... Doctor, I am so, so sorry. I can see you're having to ask me the exact same thing again, and I just feel terrible. I must be doing a dreadful job of explaining myself, or... or maybe I'm just not giving you the answer you're supposed to get? I really don't mean to be difficult, I promise. 

But... honestly, no. I really haven't had a two-week stretch like that. I always try to keep a smile on and push through, because I'd just hate to be a gloomy presence for my family or for you. 

Am I... am I misunderstanding what you're asking? Please tell me if I am. I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient and giving you exactly what you need.
